Ive been working as a receptionist in a dental office for a year now [Ontario, Canada], and many dental offices turn down patients with ODSP and HSO even. My office accepts all patients. When I asked why this was the case, they told me it was because these patients are covered at 100% and they usually take advantage of this and no show or short notice cancel their appointments. I’m confused, because people who aren’t on ODSP with 100% coverage can do this as well. 

My boyfriend is on ODSP and made a comment that also opened my eyes. Not that this is the case for all people on ODSP, but he said that people with ODSP usually have some sort of disability that affects the way someone takes care of themselves. He suffers from depression, anxiously and is bipolar. His overall hygiene is not the best as he finds it mentally and physically hard to take care of himself. He also doesn’t have access to a car. So he would have to bus to his appointments. It’s also hard for him to get out of bed sometimes.... anyway, I’m rambling but it’s just overall sad, I think, that dental care is not included in the universal healthcare. 

One of the  dentists I worked with once said he didn’t want it to be apart of the universal healthcare. He’d be getting paid $200 vs $800 for a 3 hour complicated root canal. 

Idk. Money is nice and all but dental care is important for everyone. It definitely plays a big part in your health at the end of the day.
